body.claim: A TypeScript arrow function or constant bound with const gets no symbol, so claims about them can only ever resolve while the file is byte-identical.
body.detail: codedoc-lang does not treat a lexical declaration as a naming declaration. export function f() is named; export const f = () => {} is not, and neither is export const TIMEOUT = 5000. Binding an arrow function to a const is the ordinary way to declare a function in modern TypeScript, so this is a large share of real code: measured over zod, 16.4% of imported anchors carried no symbol, against 0.0% for Java, 1.2% for C++ and 1.6% for Go. Without a symbol an anchor cannot reach rungs 2, 3, 4 or 6. The fix belongs in codedoc-lang; crates/codedoc-anchor/tests/typescript_declarations.rs holds ignored tests that will pass once it lands.
